## 🔴 BLOCKER 1 — the site says TWO episodes, the launch copy says FOUR

This is the most consequential finding of the run and it is not the newsletter.

`site/app/page.tsx` and `LatestBlueprint.tsx` read `site/data/episodes.json` **at build time**, and the site deploys from `origin/main`. The last commit on `main` is **Jul 14**. What is actually committed:

| # | slug | committed status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ai-implementation-consulting | **live** |
| 2 | voice-agent-agency | **live** |
| 3 | boring-automation-agency | upcoming |
| 4 | small-cohort-business (old numbering) | upcoming |
| 5 | solo-design-agency (old numbering) | upcoming |

The working tree has the correct file (3 live, renumbered 4=solo-design-agency), but **it was never committed** — 37 modified + 70 untracked files are sitting locally, including EP003's 7/27 site flip.

**Consequence:** the 8:30 newsletter closes on *"Four of them are up now"* and links `theoperatoreconomy.com`. The 12:30 first comment says *"Four are up."* A reader who clicks either one probably lands on a library showing **two**, with the old episode numbering.

**Verify first** (I could not fetch the site from this run): open `theoperatoreconomy.com` and count. If it shows two, the fix is:

```bash
cd /Users/manavthaker/Documents/GitHub/operator-economy
python3 studio/scripts/originate/publish.py solo-design-agency     # 4 → live
git add site/data/episodes.json
git commit -m "EP004 hour-one: site flip to live + EP003 flip backfill"
git push origin main                                                # triggers deploy
```

Do this **before 12:30** so the feed post's first comment points at four. Note `publish.py --notify` also fires the Resend email — omit `--notify` if you want the flip without the send (see §4).

## 3. 12:30 personal feed post — PASSES content-rubric-v4, AWAITING APPROVAL

Gated against `brown-man-content/content-rubric-v4.md` (not the OE post-rubric, per the rubric split).

**Cadence gate (3c-i) — measured, all seven thresholds pass:**

| Gate | Threshold | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Sentence-length CV | ≥ 0.60 | **0.77** ✓ |
| One sentence ≥ 30 words | required | **57** ✓ |
| One sentence ≤ 4 words | required | **1** ✓ |
| Fragments | ≥ 20% | **31%** ✓ |
| Conjunction starts | ≥ 8% | **11** ✓ |
| Max single opener | ≤ 15% | "the" ×4 = **11%** ✓ |
| Hedge density | ≤ 0.8/100w | **0.2** ✓ |

Package score was 92 (publish threshold 88). Voice hygiene clean: no em dashes, no banned lexicon, real personal anchor (the 1,500 florists, first-person, verified-facts safe), one exit only, no career-transition framing.

Two notes:
- **Length:** the file header says ~1,900 characters; the actual copy is **2,783**. Still well inside LinkedIn's limit, but the fold matters more than the total and the fold is strong ("For about a year I built software for fifteen hundred independent florists. / Not one of them wanted to get big.").
- **Closing question** ("What if it isn't, and the last twenty years were the weird part?") is *rewarded* under v4 §6c. It would fail the OE post-rubric. This is the personal feed, so v4 governs. Correct as written.

**First comment (fire 1:00–1:30 PM ET) — depends on Blocker 1:**

```
Been working through this one business at a time. Every Monday: one thing a single experienced person could actually build, the companies already doing it, the real stack and what it costs, honest math with the failure modes named. No income promises, no course at the end. Four are up.

theoperatoreconomy.com
```

If the site can't be fixed before 1:00, change "Four are up." to "Four are up, the fourth went live this morning." only if the site actually shows four. Otherwise drop the count entirely — a wrong number on the launch piece costs more than a vaguer sentence.

**Log it** in `first-comment-log.csv` with the URL and real post time. That log has been silent since 7/17.

## 4. Resend send — BRANDING FLAG

`publish.py --notify` sends from:

```
RESEND_FROM default: "The Operator Economy <hello@theoperatoreconomy.com>"
subject:            "№004 is live — The Design Agency You Can Run Alone"
signature:          "— The Operator Economy"
```

Per the naming split, the **site email is Operator Blueprints**; The Operator Economy is the LinkedIn newsletter. The from-name and the signature both carry the wrong product name. The body already says "The Operator Blueprint (PDF)" correctly, so it's only the wrapper.

**Fix before sending:** set `RESEND_FROM="Operator Blueprints <hello@theoperatoreconomy.com>"` in the environment, and change the signature line in `_notify_subscribers` from `— The Operator Economy` to `— Operator Blueprints`. Both are one-line edits.

Also note `content/newsletter.md` (the long-form blueprint email) still has **unresolved link placeholders**: `[Watch the full episode →]` and `[Get the blueprint →]`. If you send that version rather than the short notify email, substitute the real URLs first.

`--notify` requires `DATABASE_URL` + `RESEND_API_KEY` and prompts for confirmation before sending. I did not run it.
